Definition: Penuel or Peniel, a place East of Jordan; also (as Penuel) the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Penuel is the place east of Jordan where Jacob wrestled with God and called it Peniel, for he had seen God face to face and his life was preserved. Gideon came to Penuel and was refused bread as Succoth had refused him, and Jeroboam built Penuel when he made it his stronghold.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a place is remembered by what happened there: Jacob saw God face to face at Penuel, and no king's walls can take that away.
